subject: P06
required_fixes: P06-R4-F1 (medium): Complete pending-message recovery when a renewal fails before Conversation::drive exists. In crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:408-415, the new fail closure appends the renewal's prompt as a failed operator entry only in memory. A bootstrap error (:430-435), launcher error (:443-447), or missing pipe (:450-457) immediately returns, bypassing the final history save at :650-685. After an earlier successful turn, savedAt and saveFailure still describe that older save, but offline history omits the newly displayed failed message. The outer renewal loop has a related loss at :314-318: failure to create the next runtime home drops Launch::then without even retaining its prompt in the view. This is the same admitted-message preservation obligation as R3-F1, now remaining in pre-drive failure exits. Route these exits through common pending-work finalization so the failed prompt is durably retained with the last valid restore point, and storage failure is reported truthfully. Acceptance: complete and save a turn, make the explicit next message require renewal, then fail only the replacement engine's launch. The final view and offline protected record must contain the exact failed prompt once, with no Gateway request or replay. Also cover runtime-home creation failure before the replacement launch; an admitted prompt must not disappear there.
evidence_gaps: P06-R4-G1: The new renewal-start test stops a successfully spawned engine during its delayed initialize; drive has already placed the prompt in self.deferred, so ordinary finalization saves it. It does not exercise launcher/bootstrap/pipe failure before drive, or failure to create the next runtime home. Add production-interface failure injection for the remaining early exits and compare the final view with offline history, including truthful save status and no remote dispatch/replay. The 65 passing C20 mutation probes do not cover this boundary.
limitations: Independent read-only cumulative re-review. No source/application changes, build/test reruns, application/engine launches, product endpoint calls or credential access. The remaining finding is established by the production call graph and early-return paths, not a newly executed runtime reproduction. Only the designated verdict artifact is written.

All four supplied fingerprints independently match at the beginning and end. Reconstructed the previous source from its frozen patch, verified its hashes and inspected all six changed inputs.

R3's successful-export, held-save cancellation, queued-message and deferred-renewal paths are addressed. Pending messages now force the final save; cancellation is checked after saving and before renewal handoff; renewal prompts survive cancellation during drive startup. Four added tests cover successful delayed export, deferred/queued sends during held writes, renewal behind an export, and renewal cancellation during refresh, old-engine stop and new-engine initialization. The real-engine held-save case confirms no third Gateway request. These fixes justify restoring authority_security to 9. The remaining behavior/validation gap is pre-drive startup failure recovery.
